title: Solar PPA vs Buying Solar: Which Option Suits American Homeowners
excerpt: Understand the differences between solar Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) and buying solar panels for your home.
content:
What is a Solar PPA?

A Solar Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) is a contract between a homeowner and a solar company where the latter installs and maintains solar panels on the former's property at no upfront cost.

Buying Solar vs Solar PPA: Key Differences

Buying solar panels means purchasing the equipment outright, while a PPA involves a long-term contract with a solar company.

Pros and Cons of Each Option

Buying solar:

  • Full ownership of the solar panels
  • Durable equipment with a 25-year warranty
  • No monthly payments

Solar PPA:

  • No upfront costs or installation fees
  • Low monthly payments
  • Typically 15-25 year contracts

Conclusion

For American homeowners considering solar energy, it's essential to weigh the pros and cons of buying solar panels versus entering a Solar PPA. Research local solar companies, assess your energy needs, and consult with experts to make an informed decision that suits your lifestyle and budget.
